_comment: The Lichess puzzle-theme vocabulary this app is allowed to speak. A slug here must exist at https://lichess.org/training/<slug> — inventing one produces a 404 training link, which is worse than no link at all. Labels and descriptions are written in this repo's own words; the slug list mirrors Lichess's public theme directory. Refresh with scripts/sync_lichess_themes.py --check.

themes.label: Fork
themes.description: One piece attacks two or more enemy targets at once, so only one of them can be saved.

themes.label: Pin
themes.description: A piece cannot move without exposing something more valuable standing behind it.

themes.label: Skewer
themes.description: The mirror of a pin: the valuable piece is attacked first, and what stands behind it falls when it moves.

themes.label: Hanging Piece
themes.description: A piece is left undefended and can simply be taken.

themes.label: Discovered Attack
themes.description: Moving one piece uncovers an attack by the piece behind it on the same line.

themes.label: Discovered Check
themes.description: A discovered attack where the unveiled piece gives check, so the moving piece is free to take something.

themes.label: Double Check
themes.description: Two pieces give check at once — only a king move can answer it.

themes.label: Deflection
themes.description: A capture or threat drags a defender away from the duty it was performing. Also called overloading.

themes.label: Attraction
themes.description: An exchange or sacrifice lures an enemy piece onto a square where a follow-up tactic wins it. Also called a decoy.

themes.label: X-Ray Attack
themes.description: A piece attacks a square through an enemy piece standing on the same line.

themes.label: Clearance
themes.description: A piece or pawn deliberately vacates a square, file or diagonal so another piece can use it.

themes.label: Interference
themes.description: A piece steps between two enemy pieces and cuts the line that defended one of them.

themes.label: Intermezzo
themes.description: An in-between move played before the expected recapture, usually posing a threat that must be answered first. Also called zwischenzug.

themes.label: Capture the Defender
themes.description: The piece holding a defence together is removed, so the piece it guarded can be taken next move.

themes.label: Trapped Piece
themes.description: A piece has no safe square, so it is won by closing its escape routes rather than by force.

themes.label: Quiet Move
themes.description: A move that neither checks nor captures, preparing a threat that cannot be met.

themes.label: Sacrifice
themes.description: Material is given up in the short term to gain a decisive advantage in the forced sequence that follows.

themes.label: Promotion
themes.description: A pawn reaches the final rank; the promotion race decides many endgames.

themes.label: Underpromotion
themes.description: Promoting to a knight, bishop or rook because the queen would not win.

themes.label: En Passant
themes.description: A pawn captures an enemy pawn that has just passed it with its two-square move.

themes.label: Back-Rank Mate
themes.description: The king is trapped behind its own pawns and falls to a mate on the home rank.

themes.label: Exposed King
themes.description: A king with few defenders around it becomes the target of a direct attack.

themes.label: Kingside Attack
themes.description: An attack against a king that castled short.

themes.label: Queenside Attack
themes.description: An attack against a king that castled long.

themes.label: Smothered Mate
themes.description: A knight mates a king that is boxed in by its own pieces.

themes.label: Mate in 1
themes.description: Deliver checkmate in one move.

themes.label: Mate in 2
themes.description: Deliver checkmate in two moves.

themes.label: Mate in 3
themes.description: Deliver checkmate in three moves.

themes.label: Mate in 4
themes.description: Deliver checkmate in four moves.

themes.label: Mate in 5 or more
themes.description: A long mating sequence with no single forcing idea.

themes.label: Defensive Move
themes.description: A precise move or sequence that avoids losing material or an advantage.

themes.label: Zugzwang
themes.description: The side to move would rather pass: every legal move makes its position worse.

themes.label: Castling
themes.description: Bring the king to safety and deploy the rook for the fight ahead.

themes.label: Pawn Endgame
themes.description: An endgame with only pawns and kings, decided by opposition and passed pawns.

themes.label: Rook Endgame
themes.description: An endgame with only rooks and pawns — the most common endgame in practice.

themes.label: Knight Endgame
themes.description: An endgame with only knights and pawns.

themes.label: Bishop Endgame
themes.description: An endgame with only bishops and pawns, where the colour of the squares decides a lot.

themes.label: Queen Endgame
themes.description: An endgame with only queens and pawns.

themes.label: Advanced Pawn
themes.description: A pawn is deep in enemy territory and threatening to promote.

themes.label: Opening
themes.description: A tactic in the first phase of the game, before the pieces have sorted themselves out.

themes.label: Middlegame
themes.description: A tactic in the phase where the pieces are developed and the plans collide.

themes.label: Endgame
themes.description: A tactic in the last phase of the game.
